chunks: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj asked him:

About a man who borrows a dirham from another man and repays him a mithqal, or borrows a mithqal and repays a dirham. He said: “If it was not stipulated as a condition, then there is no harm, and that is a favor.”

“Indeed, my father عليه السلام used to borrow inferior dirhams, then from his yield he would bring good ones and say: ‘O my son, return them to the one from whom we borrowed.’ So I would say: ‘O my father, his dirhams were inferior, and these are better than them.’ Then he would say: ‘O my son, this is the favor, so give them to him.’”

key_terms.الدِّرْهَمَ: a dirham; a silver coin used here as the item borrowed or repaid
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: a voluntary favor or extra goodness beyond what is owed
key_terms.الْمِثْقَالَ: a mithqal; a weight measure, here referring to repayment value
key_terms.شَرَطَ: stipulated as a binding condition in the loan agreement
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to repay a loan with something better than what was borrowed if it was not stipulated?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that repaying a loan with something better or of different value is permissible so long as no such increase was stipulated in advance. It distinguishes voluntary excellence in repayment from forbidden usury (riba), and presents the practice of the Imam's father عليه السلام as an example of gracious conduct in financial dealings.
